blocks.explanation:
A cosine minus a sine; the formulas of this exercise need two ratios of the same kind.
We must show the difference is \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
Plan: write \(\sin 15^{\circ} = \cos 75^{\circ}\), then use \(\cos P - \cos Q\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \cos 15^{\circ} - \sin 15^{\circ}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
Method: \(\sin\theta = \cos(90^{\circ} - \theta)\), then
\[\cos P - \cos Q\]
\[= -2\sin\dfrac{P + Q}{2}\sin\dfrac{P - Q}{2}\]

Make both ratios cosines
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \cos(90^{\circ} - 15^{\circ}) = \cos 75^{\circ}\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos 15^{\circ} - \cos 75^{\circ}\]
Why: Complementary angles: the sine of an angle is the cosine of its complement.

Use the formula (\(P = 15^{\circ}\), \(Q = 75^{\circ}\))
\[= -2\sin 45^{\circ}\sin(-30^{\circ})\]
\[= 2\sin 45^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ}\]
Why: Half-sum \(\frac{90^{\circ}}{2} = 45^{\circ}\), half-difference \(\frac{-60^{\circ}}{2} = -30^{\circ}\); \(\sin(-30^{\circ}) = -\sin 30^{\circ}\).
